analysis: Integration across all 12 units found no security regression. The PR splits the CI `test-provider` lane (count 5) into per-shard lanes `test-provider-1` to `test-provider-5`, each with count 1. The route job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (head lines 43-47) requests them, and the matrix job reads `fromJSON(needs.route.outputs.routes)[format('test-provider-{0}', matrix.shard)]` (head line 142). The replayed patch confirms permissions (`contents: read`, route `permissions: {}`), triggers, secrets and action pins are unchanged. The shard values are a fixed integer matrix, so there is no attacker-controlled input in the lane-name expression. Docs in docs/developer/build.md and docs/developer/test.md only describe the new lanes and bump dates. The tests in scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (SHARDED, matrix_shards, job_lanes, requested_lanes) and scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (PROVIDER_SHARDS) assert one lane per shard and keep the existing safeguards: exact label-array grants, fallback on plane error, no `id-token` or secrets, a timeout limit, fork PRs not contacting the plane, and release workflows on literal Blacksmith runners. Provider runtime, the TB-002 wire contract, attestation and App Attest (TB-009/TB-011), cache storage (T-041), key custody and the add-on hold socket (TB-012/TB-013) are not touched, so no canonical threat-model asset or boundary is affected. Unverified contracts: the darkbloom-route.yml router and the plane were not supplied, nor was the full head of ci.yml. How the router handles the new lane names, and any difference between per-shard grants and the previous whole-lane grant, is therefore not confirmed. A mismatch there would be an availability/CI-gating issue, not a demonstrated security issue. The `provider-test-gate` job is unchanged and fails closed. The integration replay was incomplete, with 29 units omitted, which is a coverage limit rather than proof of safety.
